text:
Jori (CS): Quick alignment  we need a concise 'kickstart concierge' one-pager for customers at kickoff: prefill + batching + streaming fallbacks. Goals: reduce early churn, speed time-to-value, and detect renewal risks early. Ideas?
Aria (AE): Yes. Make it a 1-page checklist + an AE post-demo email template. Keep it action-first.
Devon (SRE): From infra: include exact knobs we expose (warm_pool_size, prefill_parallelism, batch_size caps, stream_fallback) and visible observability signals (X-Redwood-Cache, p95 latency, error-rate).
Maya (Eng-ML): Add a lightweight customer validation test (curl) with expected header so AEs can confirm cache behavior before go-live:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: tenant-123"
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?stream=true
# Expect header: X-Redwood-Cache: HIT or MISS
```
Jori (CS): Draft 48-hour customer-facing checklist (super compact):
- Day 0 (kickoff): prefill top 8-12 intents; set warm_pool_size=2-4; enable stream=true.
- Hours 0-24: watch X-Redwood-Cache header; aim for cache HIT >= 60%.
- Hours 24-48: monitor p95 and error-rate. If p95 > target or cache MISS high, follow remediation bullets below.
Remediation quick bullets (customer steps):
- cache MISS > 40%: increase prefill_parallelism to 4-8 and re-run prefill for top intents.
- p95 spike (interactive use): set batch_size=1-4 and request a warm_pool bump.
- persistent stream disconnects (>3 in 10min): flip stream to non-stream fallback route and file a support ticket with logs.
Devon (SRE): Numeric defaults we can publish for typical workloads:
- Webchat/interactive: batch_size=1-4, target_p95 <=200ms.
- High-throughput ingestion: batch_size=8-32, target_p95 <=600ms.
- Prefill parallelism: 4 workers for standard tenants, 8 for enterprise.
Aria (AE): For renewal-risk signals (include in handoff as a 14-day watch):
- Red flags: sustained p95 > threshold, cache HIT < 75% after 48h, repeated stream fallbacks, low engagement (<=10 queries/day).
- Action: schedule CS check-in, enable 48-72h warm burst, run a joint prompt audit call.
Maya (Eng-ML): Quick Python diagnostic customers can run to check cache header and stream stability:
```
import requests
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', headers={ 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + TOKEN, 'X-Redwood-Tenant': 'tenant-123' }, json={ 'input': 'ping' }, stream=True)
print('cache:', resp.headers.get('X-Redwood-Cache'))
```
Devon (SRE): Include internal ops snippet for temporary capacity requests (internal ticket template):
```
Subject: Prefill/Warm bump request 
Tenant: tenant-123
Requested: prefill_parallelism=8, warm_pool_size=6, window=72h
Reason: onboarding surge for demo week
```
Jori (CS): Plan: assemble the 1-pager + AE email templates (low-touch / high-touch) + the two diagnostic snippets. We'll pilot on next 3 customers and send a 5-question feedback survey at day 7.
Aria (AE): I'll draft the AE email with subject lines and a CTA to schedule a 30m optimization call.
Maya (Eng-ML): Add FAQ blurb about quantized variants: "If p95 > 600ms and cost sensitivity is high, ask about q4_8 quantized variants  expect ~20-30% cost savings; run A/B eval for output drift."
Jori (CS): Thanks all. CS-Bot: set reminder to review pilot feedback in 14 days.
CS-Bot: Reminder created  "Kickstart concierge one-pager draft" assigned to Jori, due in 24h.
